title: Separable split binomial roots form a scalar torsor
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\geq1$ an integer invertible in $F$, and suppose $X^n-1$ splits over $F$. Fix an algebraic closure $\Omega/F$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Write $\mu_n(F)=\{\zeta\in F^\times:\zeta^n=1\}$, with multiplication inherited from $F$. This is a finite group of cardinality $n$. For every $a\in F^\times$, the monic polynomial $X^n-a\in F[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. If $\alpha\in\Omega$ satisfies $\alpha^n=a$, then $\alpha\ne0$, and multiplication by $\alpha$ defines a bijection
$$\mu_n(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{\beta\in\Omega:\beta^n=a\},\qquad\zeta\longmapsto\alpha\zeta.$$
Moreover,
$$X^n-a=\prod_{\zeta\in\mu_n(F)}(X-\alpha\zeta)\quad\text{in }\Omega[X].$$
For $a=1$ and $\alpha=1$ this includes $X^n-1=\prod_{\zeta\in\mu_n(F)}(X-\zeta)$. No irreducibility of $X^n-a$ is assumed.

proof.text: For $b\in F^\times$ put $f_b=X^n-b$. Since $n\geq1$, this is monic of degree $n$ and $f_b'=nX^{n-1}$. Both $b$ and $n$ are invertible. The identity $-b^{-1}f_b+(nb)^{-1}Xf_b'=1$ proves separability by the Bezout definition [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. This applies to $b=a$ and $b=1$, without irreducibility.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-separable-polynomial-distinct-roots-alg-closed] to the two monic separable polynomials $f_a,f_1$ over $F$ in its algebraic closure $\Omega$. Each has exactly $n$ distinct roots, and each equals the product of $X-\rho$ over its roots in $\Omega$. All hypotheses follow from step 1 and the given algebraic closure.

proof.text: The splitting hypothesis writes $f_1=\prod_{i=1}^n(X-c_i)$ with $c_i\in F$. Evaluation at any $\gamma\in\Omega$ satisfying $\gamma^n=1$ gives $\prod_i(\gamma-c_i)=0$, hence $\gamma=c_i$ for some $i$, since $\Omega$ is a field. Thus all the $n$ roots counted in step 2 lie in $F$. They are nonzero, since $0^n=0\ne1$. Their group is precisely $\mu_n(F)$: $1^n=1$, $(uv)^n=u^nv^n=1$, and $(u^{-1})^n=(u^n)^{-1}=1$. Consequently this is a finite group of cardinality $n$.

proof.text: If $\alpha^n=a$, then $\alpha\ne0$ since $a\ne0$ and $n\geq1$. For $\zeta\in\mu_n(F)$, $(\alpha\zeta)^n=a$. Conversely, if $\beta^n=a$, then $(\beta/\alpha)^n=\beta^n/\alpha^n=1$. Step 3 places $\beta/\alpha$ in $F^\times$ and hence in $\mu_n(F)$. The formulas $\alpha(\beta/\alpha)=\beta$ and $(\alpha\zeta)/\alpha=\zeta$ show that these two maps are mutual inverses, proving the claimed bijection.

proof.text: The factorization from [lem-pc-separable-polynomial-distinct-roots-alg-closed], applied to $f_a$ as in step 2, is indexed by its distinct roots in $\Omega$. Reindex this finite product by the bijection of step 4 to obtain $X^n-a=\prod_{\zeta\in\mu_n(F)}(X-\alpha\zeta)$. Substituting $a=1$ and $\alpha=1$ gives the last asserted factorization.
